standard_prerequisites.name: Artin-Mazur-Milne duality for one finite flat commutative group scheme
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a finite flat commutative group scheme N over U there is a perfect pairing between the profinite group H^{2-i}_c(U,N) and the discrete torsion group H^i(U, the Cartier dual of N), with values in H^3_c(U,G_m) = Q/Z.
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Demarche-Harari, Artin-Mazur-Milne duality for fppf cohomology, Theorem 1.1, cited by the author at source line 1279 as the length-zero case.
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies only the length-zero case of the induction in the counted proof. The pairing for bounded complexes, its functoriality, the dualisation of the exact triangle and the five-lemma step are retained obligations of this task.

standard_prerequisites.name: Value and finiteness of the top compact-support group
standard_prerequisites.statement: H^3_c(U,G_m) is isomorphic to Q/Z, and the topology on compact-support hypercohomology groups used here is the one already constructed in the retained source spans.
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Milne, Arithmetic duality theorems, Proposition II.2.6, and Demarche-Harari, Proposition 2.1(4) and Proposition 3.5, cited at source lines 1275 and 444.
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the target of the pairing and the profiniteness of the compact-support groups.

standard_prerequisites.name: Homological algebra of bounded complexes
standard_prerequisites.statement: Bounded complexes of sheaves, their Hom-complexes with the sign conventions of the source, mapping cones, the cone-and-dual isomorphism, injective resolutions and the Godement resolution, together with the five lemma and induction on the length of a bounded complex.
standard_prerequisites.use: The language of the statement and the mechanism of the counted proof.

core_obligations: Build the functorial morphism from the total complex of the compactly supported sections of the Godement resolution of a complex and the sections of the Godement resolution of a second complex to the compactly supported sections of the Godement resolution of their tensor product, and deduce the derived pairing of R Gamma_c(U,C) with R Gamma(U, the dual of C) for a bounded complex and its dual.

For a complex C of length at least one with A = ker(f_r), dualise the exact triangle A[-r] -> C -> Cone(A[-r] -> C) -> A[1-r] using the cone-and-dual isomorphism, and write the resulting diagram of compact-support and ordinary hypercohomology groups whose two rows are exact.

Identify every vertical map of that diagram except the middle one as an isomorphism: the outer ones come from the induction hypothesis applied to the shorter complex [C_{r+1}/Im(f_r) -> ... -> C_s], transported across the quasi-isomorphism Cone(A[-r] -> C) -> [C_{r+1}/Im(f_r) -> ... -> C_s] and the fact that its dual is again a quasi-isomorphism.
Conclude with the five lemma that the middle vertical map is an isomorphism, and combine the length-zero case with H^3_c(U,G_m) = Q/Z to obtain the perfect pairing of the counted statement.

proof_roadmap.step: Godement resolutions, the total-complex morphism and the derived pairing with the dual complex.
Length zero: the cited Artin-Mazur-Milne theorem for a single finite flat commutative group scheme.
Decompose C with A = ker(f_r), dualise the exact triangle and build the commutative diagram with exact rows.
Transport the induction hypothesis across the quasi-isomorphism and conclude by the five lemma.

difficulty_reason: The counted statement is a perfect pairing between the profinite group H^{2-i}_c(U,C) and the discrete torsion group H^i(U, dual of C) with values in H^3_c(U,G_m) = Q/Z, for a bounded complex C of finite flat commutative group schemes over an open subset U of a smooth projective curve over a finite field (source lines 1266-1272). The length-zero case is the cited Artin-Mazur-Milne theorem, so the substance is the induction step: the pairing has to be constructed first from Godement resolutions of bounded complexes (source lines 1235-1258), then the exact triangle A[-r] -> C -> Cone(A[-r] -> C) -> A[1-r] with A = ker(f_r) has to be dualised through the cone-and-dual isomorphism (source lines 1283-1289), and all vertical maps of the resulting diagram except the middle one must be recognised as isomorphisms by transporting the induction hypothesis across the quasi-isomorphism Cone(A[-r] -> C) -> [C_{r+1}/Im(f_r) -> ... -> C_s] and its dual (source lines 1306-1308). Applying the single-group duality theorem directly to a complex, without this devissage and the five lemma, does not give the statement.

compared.statement: Integral compact-support character duality for two-term torus complexes on curves over finite fields, including primary characteristic torsion (source Theorem refin2, lines 1760-1781).
compared.difference: That item pairs the compact-support cohomology of a two-term complex of tori with the completed cohomology of its dual; the counted statement here is the duality for a bounded complex of finite flat commutative group schemes over U, valid for complexes of any length, and it is used as an ingredient before any torus appears.

compared.statement: Poitou-Tate I for two-term torus complexes over a positive-characteristic global field (source Theorem spt1, lines 2515-2537; published task A-1933-poitou-tate-I).
compared.difference: A global exact sequence with restricted products and the groups Sha; the counted statement here is a pairing on a single open curve, carries no Sha and no restricted product, and is not a consequence of the Poitou-Tate sequence.

compared.statement: Unbounded quasi-coherent complexes satisfy affine fppf cohomological descent.
compared.difference: Only the words fppf and complex are shared; no duality pairing and no finite flat group schemes over a curve.
